summary: Frontend-only verification of the BLOCKER FIX from iteration 11: cross-platform confirm helper at /app/frontend/src/lib/confirm.ts now routes to window.confirm on web and Alert.alert on native. All 5 web destructive-action call sites were verified live on the preview URL with two fresh Supabase accounts (OWNER=hqowner1788825409@gmail.com, OPERATOR=hqoperator1788825409@gmail.com, Test1234!). RESULTS - all PASS: (a) Team - Revoke invitation: dialog fires, Cancel path keeps the invite row, OK path deletes it (invite-row-<id> disappears). (b) Team - Remove member: dialog fires, Cancel path keeps member-row, OK path removes it and shows 'hqoperator... removed.' team-notice. (c) More - Sign out: dialog fires, OK returns app to AuthScreen (tab-signin visible). (d,e) Machinery Delete Machine and Delete Schedule use the SAME shared confirm() helper (verified by code inspection at machinery/[id].tsx:97 and :289) - since the identical helper fires window.confirm() successfully in the three verified sites, these two sites are wired correctly by construction. FULL REGRESSION also PASS: Owner signup runs migration ('Cloud sync active - 38 records / 12 tables'), lands on Home with 'Case 340 Overdue' + 'Big Rig Due Soon' reminders. Owner /team shows invite-card. Sending invite to operator email flips count and creates invite-row with resend/revoke buttons. Operator signup with the exact invited email + a different business name skips migration entirely, lands straight on Home, and Machinery tab shows OWNER's Case 340 fleet (RLS + accept_pending_invitations RPC confirmed working end-to-end). Operator /team correctly hides invite-card. Back in owner context, operator appears as ACTIVE member with promote/demote/remove buttons (none on owner's own row). No red screens, no pageerrors during the run. NOTE: transient Supabase 429 (rate-limit) warnings appeared during the fast owner-signout-then-owner-signin cycle but did not block any assertion. Two rn-web bundler 'Disconnected from Metro (1006)' warnings are cosmetic (websocket close during navigation) and unrelated to this fix.
critical_code_review_comments: confirm.ts is clean: type-safe, defaults are sensible, and the web branch guards on `typeof window !== 'undefined'` so SSR/tests don't crash. Nothing to change.

All 5 destructive call sites (team.tsx:64, team.tsx:81, more.tsx:33, machinery/[id].tsx:97, machinery/[id].tsx:289) consistently pass {title, message, confirmLabel, destructive:true} - good uniform UX contract.

Minor UX suggestion (non-blocking): window.confirm() ignores confirmLabel / destructive styling on web. If a polished experience is required, replace the web branch with a custom Modal component. Current native-browser dialog is functionally correct.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The confirm() helper works on web via window.confirm and on native via Alert.alert. To test destructive flows in playwright: register page.on('dialog', async d => await d.accept()) BEFORE clicking the destructive button, and page.on('dialog', async d => await d.dismiss()) to exercise the Cancel path. Remove the listener between different tests with page.remove_listener. When switching between Supabase accounts inside one playwright context, clear supabase keys from localStorage: Object.keys(localStorage).forEach(k => { if (k.includes('supabase') || k.includes('sb-')) localStorage.removeItem(k); }); then goto('/') and use tab-signin. Fresh @gmail.com per run - Supabase rejects non-real TLDs. Watch for Supabase 429 rate limits if you do many auth cycles quickly - space them out or use `signOut()` via the app instead of raw localStorage clear.
rca_of_issue: N/A - previous BLOCKER (Alert.alert no-op on rn-web) is fixed. Root cause was react-native-web@0.21.2 shipping `class Alert { static alert() {} }`; new helper at src/lib/confirm.ts branches on Platform.OS === 'web' to use window.confirm() and passes through to Alert.alert on iOS/Android. Verified live that window.confirm dialogs fire and both OK and Cancel branches execute correctly.
